before: The order of concurrent split siblings read only the text each new paragraph copies. When a paragraph of such a run was deleted, a paragraph split off it that held other text could move after its sibling.
after: A paragraph that a split creates records, in its shared record field splitPoints, the paragraph it split and the identity of the first character it moved, after the split points of the paragraph it split (at most four); any other paragraph an edit creates, as a break at a paragraph's end, takes the split points of the paragraph listed right before it. The order of concurrent split siblings compares the nearest split of one paragraph two blocks both name, by where those first moved characters stand in the text they came from, and reads the copied text only when they name none in common or the same character. A paragraph split off a deleted sibling keeps that sibling's place.
reason: The field is a new key on a paragraph record that the peer creating the paragraph writes once, in the transaction that creates it, so no two peers write it. Released readers would not read it and would order the run by text alone, which is the repairVersion 3 change these records already make; replicas with repairVersion 2 refuse these rooms. A paragraph without the field, as a release without it wrote, falls back to the text rule, so rooms of this format created before the field order as before. sharedSchemaVersion does not change: the field is an optional key on a record that replicas of this format write once and others only read, no existing field changes meaning, and a paragraph without it orders by the earlier rule.
